## 2. Objective (condensed, complete)

Common rules (from `scratchpad\WORKER-BRIEF.md`, which you should also read):
- Work only in the worktree. Stay in owned paths (below). Do NOT edit `src/lib/capabilities/**` or `src/app/api/platform/v1/**` (broker worker owns them): if a broker change is needed, describe it in the handoff. Contracts fixed: `controlplane/types.ts`, `digest.ts`, `capabilities/catalog.ts`, `resources/types.ts`, `drivers/types.ts`, `credentials/types.ts`, `tofu/types.ts`, `policy/types.ts`, `observability/types.ts`, `machines/types.ts`, `workflows/types.ts`, `placement/types.ts`, `incidents/types.ts`, `docs/platform/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/platform/RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/adr/*.md`.
- No dependency changes (no `npm install`, no `package.json` edits). Do not touch `src/lib/providers/localstack/**`; LocalStack is ON HOLD (never routed to the workflow path, no LocalStack code/tests).
- Honesty (spec 42): never claim a test passed that you did not run; never label mocked behaviour as real; say what is unverified live (nothing here has touched a real AWS account; no credentials exist on this machine).
- Security: no secret values anywhere (manifests, revisions, audit, events, logs, errors, responses); no secret INPUT fields on connection actions; every tenant row scoped by workspace; external strings are data.
- Style: TS strict; module-top doc comments stating invariants and honest limits; `@/lib/...` imports; no import cycles; `src/lib` never imports `@/app`; do not name non-hook helpers `use*`; files < ~600 lines; Vitest tests are `*.test.ts` under `tests/bridge/`.
- Windows 11. Bash tool = Git Bash; PowerShell too. Node 24. Do not use ports 4566, 54329, 7233, 8181 (another project's containers `ssc-*`). Zenith's own Postgres for gated tests: `<redacted-credential-url>/zenith_platform` (not needed here).

**Design source:** `docs/adr/0001-evolve-not-rewrite.md`: the existing engine keeps running sandbox (and LocalStack); real providers run through Temporal workflows (ADR-0009) that project progress onto the SAME `Deployment` records the UI already renders. Also read ADR 0006/0007/0009, `docs/platform/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**Owned paths:** `src/lib/bridge/**` (new); `src/lib/actions/defs/deploy.ts`, `promote.ts`, `connection.ts` (minimal edits); `src/lib/actions/defs/connection-aws.ts` (new, and register it in `src/lib/actions/defs/index.ts` with `import "./connection-aws";`, a one-line edit that is needed and was not forbidden); `src/lib/engine/engine.ts` (minimal); `src/lib/providers/aws/provider.ts` (availability/labels/preflight text only); `src/lib/domain/types.ts` (ADDITIVE optional fields only); `tests/bridge/**`; plus existing tests of those files (update only when behaviour intentionally changes, and say so).

3. **`src/lib/bridge/deploy.ts`** (the core; keep < 600 lines, split if needed):
   - `executionRoute(env)` -> one of `{kind:"engine"}`, `{kind:"unlinked"}`, `{kind:"not_ready", readiness}`, `{kind:"unverified"}`, `{kind:"workflow", provider, readiness, connection}`. Rules: provider (from `q.connection(env.connectionId)?.provider ?? "sandbox"`) not in `REAL_PROVIDERS` -> engine. Linked -> `await deps.readiness(provider)`; not ready -> `not_ready`; ready but `deps.platformConnection(...)` is not `verified` -> `unverified` ("run connection.verifyAws"); else `workflow`.
   - Check planning (plan mode): `broker.check({ capability: "deployment.deploy", scope: {workspaceId, projectId, environmentId}, input: {} }, principalFromAction(ctx), { via })`; add the decision (outcome + reason messages + approval requirement) to `plan.details`; `deny` -> `blocked` with the reasons; `require_approval` -> `requiresApproval: true`; map a thrown `BrokerError` to `blocked` (message + `fix`); never throw out of plan. `principalFromAction` is exported from `@/lib/capabilities/action-bridge`.
   - Start (`startWorkflowDeployment`): (a) revision snapshot stays in `deploy.ts` exactly as today (before this call); (b) mint `deploymentId = id()`; (c) `broker.propose({ capability: "deployment.deploy", scope, input: { revisionId, deploymentId }, idempotencyKey: "bridge-deploy-"+deploymentId, reason?: message }, principalFromAction(ctx), { via: "ui"|"navigator"|"mcp", cost: { deltaUsdMonthly: changeset.totalCostDeltaUsd, projectedUsdMonthly: changeset.projectedMonthlyUsd } })`. Input carries ids only (never anything from the manifest). (d) create the `Deployment` (`executor: "workflow"`, `operationId`, `steps: plannedWorkflowSteps()`, `previousRevisionId: env.deployedRevisionId`, `actor: ctx.actor`, `changeSummary`, `estCostDeltaUsd`), push to `db().deployments`, `save(projectId)`, emit a `status` event. (e) branch on `result.decision.outcome` / `result.operation.status`:
     - `deny`: Deployment `failed`, `error` = reason messages (policy reasons), pending steps skipped; return `ok:false` with the reasons.
     - `require_approval` (op `awaiting_approval`): Deployment status `awaiting_approval`; `data` carries `{ deploymentId, operationId, proposalDigest, status, approval: "/api/platform/v1/operations/<id>" pointer }`; NO workflow started.
     - `allow` (op `approved`) AND `env.policies.approvalRequired` (the product's own approval policy; the broker does not read it): Deployment `awaiting_approval`, no workflow; `deploy.approve` later runs the product gate (admin role, `approvalSeparation`) and then starts it. Keep this: an approval policy must not be walkable-around.
     - `allow` and no product approval: start now: `broker.beginExecution({ workspaceId, operationId, holder: "workflow:"+operationId, audience: "worker", leaseMs: 5*60_000 })` (holder MUST equal ws-act's `executionHolder` = `workflow:<operationId>` because its heartbeat uses that holder; ws-act's `CLAIM_LEASE_MS` is 5 min), discard the returned compact grant (never log or store it), then `workflows.startDeploy({ operationId, workspaceId, projectId, environmentId, revisionId, deploymentId, connectionId: env.connectionId, preApproved: true, build: <true when any managed service has a source build; else false> })`, set `d.workflowStartedAt`, status stays `planning` (the worker projects further). `connectionId` is the LEGACY `env.connectionId` because the worker resolves the platform connection by that id (see decision 3 below).
     - startDeploy failure after beginExecution: nothing is running; call `broker.completeExecution({ outcome: "failed", error })` (or `markUncertain` for an ambiguous timeout: `TemporalUnavailableError` whose message ends "timed out"), fail the Deployment with an honest message, return `ok:false`.
   - `approveWorkflowDeployment(ctx, d)`: refuse non-browser actors (no proof) with a sentence naming the fix (use the web app; the platform approval route is browser-only). Resolve op via `broker.getOperationDetail`. If op `awaiting_approval`: `broker.approve({ workspaceId, operationId, proposalDigest: op.proposalDigest, approver: {kind:"user", id, name}, session })` (map `BrokerError`s: `separation_of_duties`, `approver_role_insufficient`, `digest_mismatch`, `operation_expired`, ... to `ok:false` + `fix`). Then: if `!d.workflowStartedAt` -> run the start sequence (`beginExecution` + `startDeploy`); else -> `workflows.signalApproval(operationId)` (the workflow is parked at its plan-level approval gate: it suspended running -> awaiting_approval and re-verifies through `checkApproval`). If op already `approved` and `!workflowStartedAt` (product-approval-only case): apply product separation rules then start. If op `running` and started: idempotent "already underway". Keep requester/approver separation (`approvalSeparation` in deploy.ts) for production exactly as for engine deployments.
   - `cancelWorkflowDeployment(ctx, d)`: op `awaiting_approval|approved|queued` (workflow not started) -> `broker.cancelOperation({ workspaceId, operationId, principal, reason })`, then mark the Deployment `cancelled` yourself (nobody else will: skip pending steps, `endedAt`, event, release lease). Op `running` -> `workflows.cancelOperation(operationId)` (signal); the worker projects `cancelled` through its product port; report `delivered:false/not_found` honestly (the DB row is truth). Terminal -> refuse with the existing sentence.
   - Rollback/promote (`startWorkflowRollback`): same as start but capability `deployment.rollback`, input `{ revisionId: target.id, deploymentId }` (the worker's context loader reads `revisionId`/`deploymentId` from `proposal.input`), `changeSummary: "Roll back to r<n>"`, still the deploy workflow (`startDeploy`; there is no separate rollback workflow). Do NOT set `rollbackOf` on workflow deployments and do NOT flip the origin deployment to `rolling_back` (the worker's product port never settles it; it would stick). Keep the existing `statefulDeletionBlock` guard on this path.

## 6. Decisions and assumptions already made (do not undo)

1. Real-provider routing requires BOTH a platform-linked connection (`platformConnectionId`) and readiness and a verified platform connection; legacy Preview AWS connections (no platform link) cannot execute anything (no role ARNs exist) and keep the unchanged Preview refusal, without probing readiness.
2. The broker is the only approval authority for infrastructure; additionally the product's `env.policies.approvalRequired` is still honoured for workflow deployments (parked `awaiting_approval`, `deploy.approve` runs the product gate, admin role + production requester/approver separation, then starts). `deploy.approve` for a workflow deployment never calls `engine.approve`.
3. Platform `ProviderConnection` id = legacy `CloudConnection` id (create with `repos.connections.create({ id, legacyConnectionId })` and set `platformConnectionId` to it). Reason: ws-act's activities resolve `connections.resolve({ connectionId: ctx.product.environment.connectionId })`, i.e. by the environment's legacy id; one id works regardless of how its adapter maps ids.
4. Bridge calls `beginExecution` itself (as the orchestrator specified) with holder `workflow:<operationId>`; the ws-act workflow's `markOperation("running")` is then a no-op because the op is already running, and its heartbeats use that same holder. Trade-off to report: if the worker is down the claim lease (5 min) lapses and the ledger reconciler marks the op `uncertain`; the alternative (not claiming in the bridge and letting the workflow's `markOperation` claim an `approved` op) is more robust. Offer it to the orchestrator as a follow-up; do not switch silently.
5. Rollback is the same deploy workflow with capability `deployment.rollback` (no rollback workflow exists). Flag to the orchestrator: verify the credential broker's session policy (`src/lib/credentials/aws/session-policy.ts`) and ws-act's activities accept `deployment.rollback` as the operation capability for plan/apply, since they request weaker capabilities (`infrastructure.plan` for plans) per operation.
6. Planned step list = the deploy workflow's declared sequence including `build` (the workflow records it `skipped` when images are pinned) and `approval` (recorded `skipped` when policy allows).
7. The engine treats a TERMINAL workflow deployment's stale environment lease like any other (cleaned up), because the worker's product port both claims (`claimActive`, only if free) and CAS-checks (`commitOutcome`) `activeDeploymentId`; a stale lease would otherwise make every later workflow deployment end `cancelled: superseded`.
8. The readiness `drivers` check reads this process's driver registry (`listDrivers(provider)` from `@/lib/drivers/types`). On a split deployment (web on Vercel, drivers only imported by the worker) it will report no drivers until the web process imports them. Report this to the orchestrator as an integration decision (import the driver module in the control plane, or attest differently); do not hide it.
9. `ProviderId` in `domain/types.ts` (`sandbox|localstack|aws|kubernetes|gcp|azure`) is left alone (no `oci`/`zenith` yet); `REAL_PROVIDERS` is a superset so routing is ready for them.
10. Provider `availability` becoming a getter means `src/app/api/bootstrap/route.ts` (not ours) caches its provider projection keyed on registry identity+size, so the shell will keep showing `preview` until restart. Report to the orchestrator: that projection must not memoize `availability`/`tagline` (or must key on them).
11. Items to report as contract/integration asks (do not implement outside owned paths): `ActionContext` browser marker (see step 1 `browserSession`); bootstrap projection caching (decision 10); optional broker follow-ups: none required so far; env vars involved: `ZENITH_PLATFORM_DB[_URL]`, `ZENITH_TEMPORAL_ADDRESS|NAMESPACE|API_KEY|TLS`, `ZENITH_CONTROL_SIGNING_JWK|KMS_KEY_ID`, `ZENITH_OIDC_SIGNING_JWK|KMS_KEY_ID`, `ZENITH_OIDC_ISSUER`, `ZENITH_PLATFORM_BROKER_MEMORY` (must be unset: readiness refuses an in-memory broker store because the worker cannot see it).
12. Nothing was exercised against a real AWS account, real STS or a real Temporal worker; say so in the final handoff. The readiness `temporal` check proves the server answers, not that a worker polls the queue.
